visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A large, round, spiky yellowish-green fruit identified as Darap sits prominently on a green plastic bag in the center of a dining table. A woman with long hair tied back with a bow headband, wearing a grey t-shirt and black shorts, stands behind the table. Several men are seated around the table, which is covered with a red floral cloth and holds plates of food, a bottle of water, and a red soda can. (2) The scene briefly cuts to a man in a black and white striped shirt attempting to bite or press his forehead into the spiky exterior of the fruit as a humorous stunt while others watch in an indoor setting with yellowish wallpaper. (3) The woman uses both hands to pull apart the thick, spiky skin of the fruit, revealing a white, fleshy, and stringy interior filled with numerous white segments. The camera remains at a medium-close shot focusing on her hands and the fruit's texture as she explains the process to the viewers. (4) The woman picks up a segment of the white flesh, places it in her mouth, and tastes it while looking directly at the camera with an expressive facial expression. A man in a black t-shirt stands in the background near a doorway, observing the scene in the brightly lit room. (5) The video concludes with a graphical overlay featuring a circular portrait of the woman smiling, surrounded by autumn leaf illustrations and social media interaction icons for liking, subscribing, and sharing against a dark background.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video aims to introduce and review a unique regional fruit called Darap (Marang) found in Sabah, Malaysia. It demonstrates the fruit's appearance, a humorous method of opening it, and provides a sensory review of its taste and texture for viewers, emphasizing its rarity in places like Taiwan.
